name_reason: Compliant with data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain 'battle' (battle/progression core table), descriptor 'spell_bit_mask_lookup_table' accurately conveys spell-related single-bit mask lookup table. No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix matching its own/any address). Datatype role (lookup table) reflected in name.
purpose: Lookup table mapping a bit index (0..7) to its single-bit mask, used to set a spell's bit in the per-character spells_known bitmap when a spell is learned.
logic_summary: 8-byte const table where element[i] = 1 << i, i.e. {1,2,4,8,0x10,0x20,0x40,0x80}. Sole reader fd2_grant_spell_to_char copies the whole table to a local (machine code MOVSD-to-stack), then ORs table[spell_id % 8] into spells_known_bitmap[spell_id / 8] to mark spell_id learned. Since the table is exactly {1<<0 .. 1<<7}, the indexed read equals 1 << (spell_id % 8).
element_semantics: element[i] = 1 << i (single-bit mask for bit position i, i in 0..7).
notes: src comment block (spellsel.c lines 63-66) is already accurate and concise (states single-bit mask per bit index, address @0x52024, the 8 values = 1<<n, sole reader, and the MOVSD-to-stack local-copy detail), so comment_verdict=keep, no Edit to src. Ghidra plate was blank (PLATE=null) so per the blank-plate rule a concise data plate was created via run_script_inline + cu.setComment(PLATE_COMMENT,...) and the program was saved. Verified xrefs: only fd2_grant_spell_to_char READs this 8-byte table; zero writers => const confirmed. The adjacent table at 0x5202c (bytes 0f 0f 0f 0f 07 03 01 00, read by fd2_animate_spell_projectile_paths) is a SEPARATE table beyond this byte[8] boundary, not a reader of this symbol.
